name: Cardarine (GW501516)
lead: Cardarine, also known as GW501516, GW-1516 and Endurobol, is an experimental drug that selectively activates the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor delta (PPAR-delta). It was developed by Ligand Pharmaceuticals and GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) as a possible treatment for dyslipidemia and metabolic disease, and GSK stopped development in 2007 [1][2]. It was later found to cause cancer in several organs in rodents at high doses, according to Wikipedia [1][3].

It is not a hormone or a SARM, although it is sold and discussed alongside SARMs. In looksmaxxing forums it is used for fat loss and endurance, mostly in leanmaxxing and cutting plans [4][5][6]. Small randomized trials in healthy volunteers and in people with obesity or dyslipidemia reported effects on triglycerides, HDL cholesterol and fat oxidation, while no trial has tested it for appearance outcomes in healthy people [7][8][9][10]. The World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited it in 2009 and warned in 2013 about health risks [1].
infobox: Unapproved; scheduled in Australia (2018); unscheduled in the US and UK [1]

paras: GW501516 is a selective agonist of PPAR-delta, a nuclear receptor that acts as a sensor of dietary lipids and regulates fatty acid and carbohydrate metabolism [11]. In muscle cells it increases expression of genes for fatty-acid transport, beta-oxidation and mitochondrial respiration, and in animals it attenuated features of metabolic syndrome [12][13]. Because it was reported to mimic aspects of exercise signalling, reviews list PPAR-delta agonists among "exercise mimetics" [14]. In mice given high doses, Ronald Evans's laboratory reported large gains in physical endurance, according to Wikipedia [1]. Human muscle studies have also examined PPAR-delta and AMP kinase in lipid and glucose handling [15]. In obese monkeys it raised HDL and lowered VLDL [1].

GSK carried the compound through phase I and II trials for dyslipidemia before stopping [2][1]. A randomized trial in healthy volunteers examined effects on triglycerides and HDL cholesterol [7]. A randomized, double-blind, crossover trial of six-week treatment periods tested GW501516 against placebo on lipoprotein metabolism in dyslipidemic men with central obesity [8]. A 2008 randomized trial in moderately obese men reported that PPAR-delta activation was associated with reversal of multiple metabolic abnormalities, less oxidative stress and increased fatty acid oxidation [9]. A trial in people with low HDL cholesterol and features of metabolic syndrome examined lipid effects [10]. A review notes that, after clinical trials in diabetes, GSK announced that research would stop because preclinical rodent studies linked the drug to widespread tumour development [16].
None of these trials had body weight, body fat or physique in healthy people as its focus, and no study has tested the doses or durations described in looksmaxxing forums.

The main documented concern is cancer in animals. GSK is reported to have found rapid cancer development in multiple organs in mice and rats at a dose of 3 mg/kg per day [1]. A mouse study found that activation of PPAR-delta accelerated intestinal adenoma growth [17], and a 2018 mouse study linked GW501516 to faster growth of colitis-associated colorectal cancer, according to Wikipedia [1]. A review of PPARbeta/delta agonists describes the tumour findings as the reason for GSK discontinuing research [16]. No long-term human safety data are available.

A 2024 case report described reversible gynecomastia and hypogonadism in a user of a commercial performance-enhancing supplement; the report concerns supplement products as a group and its relevance to cardarine specifically depends on the product's contents [18].

Ligand and GSK collaborated from 1992 on PPAR compounds, and GW501516 was described in a 2001 PNAS paper that reported selective PPAR-delta activation promoting reverse cholesterol transport [1][19]. A 2006 review described GlaxoSmithKline and Ligand as developing it for dyslipidemia, with phase II trials ongoing [2]. GSK dropped development in 2007, and later animal testing showed cancer [1]. Concern about its use by athletes emerged before the 2008 Beijing Olympics; WADA prohibited it in 2009 and in 2013 warned that clinical approval has not and will not be given for it [1].

Cardarine is unapproved as a drug. Australia scheduled it as illegal in 2018, while the US and UK list it as unscheduled [1]. Several athletes, including cyclists, a race walker, a boxer and a sprinter, have tested positive for it [1]. Natural bodybuilding organisations list it among prohibited substances [20].

On looksmax.org, cardarine appears in threads from teenagers and young men planning to lose fat quickly, in comparisons with clenbuterol, and in combinations with HGH and other compounds [4][5][6][21][22]. One thread title argues that anyone not taking cardarine while leanmaxxing is "not even trying" [22]. A reply to a 17-year-old asking about it jokingly renamed it "Cancerine" [4]. On T Nation, it is listed in multi-SARM stacks and cycles [20][23].

lore.intro: Cardarine is discussed on looksmax.org as a fat-loss and endurance add-on for leanmaxxing, often alongside other drugs, with recurring jokes and warnings about cancer [4][22].

claims.claim: Cardarine helps you get lean quickly
claims.believers: Posters planning cuts, including teenagers, say they intend to use it alone or with diet; a title argues it is essential to leanmaxxing [4][21][22].
claims.experts: Small randomized trials report improved triglycerides, HDL and fatty acid oxidation in volunteers with dyslipidemia or obesity, but fat loss in healthy people has not been the studied outcome [7][8][9].

claims.claim: It is a milder option than clenbuterol
claims.believers: A looksmax.org user said clenbuterol side effects are bad and GW is better, while noting that clenbuterol is stronger [6].
Forum users joke about "Cancerine" and warn about risk [4].
claims.experts: GSK stopped development after rodent studies linked the drug to widespread tumours, and a mouse study linked PPAR-delta activation to faster adenoma growth; no human cancer data exist [16][17][1].

claims.believers: It is marketed as Endurobol and discussed as an endurance aid.
claims.experts: Large performance gains were reported in mice at high doses; human endurance trials are not reported in the sources reviewed. WADA prohibits it as performance enhancing [1].

card.summary: A discontinued metabolic drug sold as a fat-loss and endurance aid; some lipid benefits in small trials, but rodent cancer findings ended its development.
card.note: Rodent studies found cancer in several organs; banned in sport; no approved use.

quick.overview:
Cardarine is an experimental drug that activates PPAR-delta, a receptor that turns up fat burning in muscle. GSK developed it for cholesterol and metabolic disease and then stopped in 2007.

Small human trials showed better triglycerides, HDL and fat oxidation, but none was designed to test weight or fat loss in healthy people. It is sold alongside SARMs and used by some in cuts.
quick.mechanism: It selectively activates PPAR-delta, which raises expression of genes for fatty acid transport and oxidation in muscle and has been described as mimicking some effects of exercise.
quick.risks: Rodent studies found tumour development in several organs, which led GSK to halt research. There are no long-term human safety data. It is banned by WADA and unapproved, and some countries such as Australia have scheduled it.
